mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the forecast period reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thus producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the identified tightening episode, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression controlling for macro factors.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 5% for two consecutive months is accompanied by a decline in monthly employment (PAYEMS), signaling labor market cooling that reduces investor confidence and drives negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% for two consecutive months AND PAYEMS < previous month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a two-way F-test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) exceeding 2% above the prior month's level coincides with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO), suggesting an over-heating demand cycle that raises short-term equity valuations and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative or the interaction is not robust (p > 0.05) in a Granger causality test.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 3% for three consecutive months indicates weakening supply capacity, which raises the scarcity premium on equities and produces positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive return over the 60-day horizon during identified contraction episodes, or the effect is spurious (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to market anticipation of aggressive rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or the inflation signal is not predictive (p > 0.05) in a regression with lagged returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in unemployment proxies (UNRATE) below 4% for a single month, without a corresponding rise in payrolls (PAYEMS), suggests a strengthening labor market that depresses equity valuations and yields negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND PAYEMS does not increase
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in retail activity (HOUST) with a second derivative greater than zero (i.e., upward concavity) while industrial production lags suggests momentum-driven optimism in consumer demand, pushing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: Second difference of HOUST > 0 in the current month
failure_condition: No significant positive return over 20 days, or the acceleration is not statistically detectable (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in manufacturing activity (INDPRO) of 10% or more over three consecutive months indicates persistent supply-side weakness, which amplifies equity risk premia and results in positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive returns during the contraction, or the relationship is not robust (p > 0.05).
